issue.title: fix(deep-link): hit Funnelcake REST before relays for /video/<id>
issue.body:
Closes #4178

## Summary

- Cold-start `divine.video/video/<sha256>` deep-links were stuck behind a generic spinner for 60s+ before rendering. Reorders `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` to local cache → Funnelcake REST → relay (each capped by a 3s timeout), so the canonical REST source answers first instead of running last after two relay round-trips that wait for EOSE from disconnected relays.
- Swaps the deep-link loading state from a generic Material `CircularProgressIndicator` to `BrandedLoadingIndicator` (matches the rest of the app).

## Why this was slow

`_VideoRouteCandidate.parse` treats a 64-char hex routeId as **both** an event id and a stable id. The previous flow ran:

1. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(ids:[hash], …)])` — never matches for Blossom-hashed share URLs (kind 34236 event ids are computed differently, the URL hash is the d-tag).
2. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(d:[hash], …)])` — may match.
3. Funnelcake REST.

`NostrClient.queryEvents` waits for EOSE from every relay in the pool with a 5s default timeout, and any relay still mid-connect during cold start blocks the whole batch. The on-relay-ready retry in `VideoDetailScreen` then re-runs the entire sequence on first relay connection. Worst case: ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake + relay-ready wait + ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake = comfortably 60s.

REST is now first because it answers in <1s without waiting on relay state and is the canonical source for divine.video share URLs. Relay is kept as a fallback so events that only live on a user's personal relay still resolve.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/video_detail_screen_test.dart` — 11/11 pass (including updated `BrandedLoadingIndicator` assertions and the cold-start retry test)
- [x] `flutter test packages/videos_repository/` — 322/322 pass, including 4 new `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` tests:
  - resolves shared stable IDs via Funnelcake REST without hitting relay
  - falls back to relay when REST returns null (event only on personal relay)
  - falls back to relay when REST throws (e.g. `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`)
  - returns null without blocking when relay queries hang past the route timeout (verifies the in-source 3s cap fires)

issue.title: feat(auth): add under-16 family guidance flow
issue.body:
Closes #3532

## Summary
This PR adds the client-side under-16 family guidance flow.

It is intentionally scoped to mobile UX only:
- a new welcome-screen entry point
- a deep-linkable `/account-review` flow
- an under-13 parent-or-guardian email path
- a 13-15 parental consent path that tells families to record the video outside the app and email it to `support@divine.video`

This PR does **not** add moderation backend wiring, private in-app video submission, or any DM-based consent-video flow.

## What Changed
- adds a new welcome CTA: `Not 16 yet? That's OK. Here's what you can do.`
- adds a public `account-review` route family that works from welcome or a moderation deep link later
- adds a shared explainer screen about regional rules and Divine's family-guidance approach
- adds an under-13 screen that directs parents or guardians to email `support@divine.video`
- adds a 13-15 screen that explains the parental consent video requirements and makes the path explicitly email-only
- adds deep-link parsing for `https://divine.video/account-review?source=...`
- adds focused router, deep-link, and widget tests for the new flow

## Product Boundaries In This PR
- Under 13: parent or guardian must email support. No in-app workaround.
- Age 13 to 15: the parental consent video must be recorded outside the app and emailed to support.
- Under no circumstances should a parental consent video be posted on Divine.
- DM can be wired later for moderation/support communication, but this PR does not claim that DM is a safe path for sending the video itself.

## Not Included
- moderation case creation or server state
- restricted-account enforcement from backend signals
- private media upload or encrypted video attachment support
- moderator tooling in other repos

## Main Files
- `mobile/lib/screens/auth/welcome_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_under13_support_screen.dart`

issue.title: context.watch causing unnecessary widget rebuilds

labels.name: performance
labels.description: App startup, video playback, rendering, and memory

issue.body:
**Problem**

Some widgets use `context.watch<SomeBloc>()` to subscribe to an entire BLoC state but only read 1 field, causing rebuilds whenever any unrelated state field changes. `context.select` (or `BlocSelector`) should be used to subscribe to only the needed property.

**Evidence (examples)**

1. **`profile_videos_grid.dart` line 199**: `context.watch<BackgroundPublishBloc>()` watches the full state but only uses `.state.uploads` (filtered to active ones). `BackgroundPublishState` emits on every upload progress tick (progress field changes per upload). The grid rebuilds on every tick even though it only cares about which uploads exist and whether they have a result. This is the highest-impact occurrence because progress updates are frequent during upload.

2. **`video_editor_draw_item_indicator.dart` line 18**: `context.watch<VideoEditorDrawBloc>().state.selectedTool` watches full state but only reads `selectedTool`. `VideoEditorDrawState` has 7 fields. The indicator rebuilds when undo/redo availability, color, or stroke width change, none of which affect it.

3. **`profile_header_widget.dart` line 73**: `context.watch<MyProfileBloc>().state` watches a sealed class with 5 variants but only pattern-matches the `profile` field from `MyProfileUpdated`. Rebuilds on loading-to-loaded transitions, `isFresh` changes, `extractedUsername` changes, and error states, all irrelevant to the header's rendering.

**Done well**

`comment_item.dart` uses `BlocSelector<CommentsBloc, CommentsState, ({bool isUpvoted, bool isDownvoted, ...})>` to select exactly the 4 vote-related fields. `comments_screen.dart` uses `BlocSelector<CommentsBloc, CommentsState, CommentsSortMode>`. `my_followers_screen.dart` uses `BlocSelector<MyFollowingBloc, MyFollowingState, bool>`. These demonstrate the correct pattern.

**Impact**

Medium. #1 has the most room for improvement since upload progress emits many times per second during active uploads, triggering full grid rebuilds. #2 and #3 cause extra rebuilds on moderately interactive screens. None cause visible jank in isolation, but they add up and are worth addressing to keep new code on the right track.

**Effort**

Low. Each fix is a one-line change from `context.watch<Bloc>()` to `context.select<Bloc, T>((bloc) => bloc.state.field)`.

**Source**: [Code Review — Performance](docs/code-review/issues-performance.md)

comment.body: @realmeylisdev Actually, I observed it even without any active upload, so it's not directly caused by `context.watch<BackgroundPublishBloc>()`. However, it's still something we should improve as well.

Quick self-review pass on top of 765a29d while it's warm — pushed two more refinements as **caafd0a9f**, both in service of consistency between the route helpers:

1. **Documented why `_fetchAddressableVideoFromRelay` doesn't duplicate the Funnelcake fallback** that `getVideosByAddressableIds` does internally. issue.title: fix(perf): cache BlurhashDisplay decode future across rebuilds
issue.body:
## Description

`BlurhashDisplay` constructed a fresh `_createImageFromPixels(...)` future inside its `build()` method. Each parent rebuild created a new `Future` (different identity), so `FutureBuilder` treated it as a fresh request and re-showed the gradient fallback while the new decode completed. On a 50+ tile profile grid churning under `BackgroundPublishBloc` upload-progress emissions (tracked in #3605), this multiplied into visible flicker across the whole grid plus redundant `decodeImageFromPixels` calls per visible tile.

This was surfaced on low-end Android in @hm21's [review of PR #4191](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4191#pullrequestreview-4257933582), as one of three layers of residual jank that PR's `memCacheWidth` cap didn't address.

### Fix

Cache the decode future in `State` so its identity stays stable across rebuilds, and recompute it only when `blurhash` / `contentType` actually change:

- New `Future<ui.Image?>? _imageFuture` field on `_BlurhashDisplayState`.
- `_decodeBlurhash()` now constructs the future once when new `BlurhashData` arrives, alongside `_blurhashData`, inside the existing `setState`.
- `build()` reads `_imageFuture` instead of constructing a new one each call.

Single-file production change (+12 / -6). Test added pinning the new invariant.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4196

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib/widgets/blurhash_display.dart test/widgets/blurhash_display_test.dart` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/blurhash_display_test.dart` — 1/1 pass (new test asserts `same(future)` across a parent rebuild).
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail_test.dart test/widgets/video_thumbnail_widget_test.dart` — 20/20 pass (existing tests that exercise `BlurhashDisplay` via its callers).
- [ ] Manual: open a profile with **50+ videos** + an active upload (own profile). Confirm gradient fallback no longer flickers across grid tiles during upload-progress ticks. Compare against `main`.

## Related (not addressed here)

- #3605 — `context.watch<BackgroundPublishBloc>` rebuilding the whole grid on every progress tick (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz). Reducing rebuild frequency is the bigger lever; this PR makes each rebuild cheaper while waiting for that fix.
- #3603 — Move profile grid de-duplication out of `build()` (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz).
- #4191 — `memCacheWidth` cap on the network image (decode-cache thrash). Independent layer of the same lag report.

## Summary
This PR adds the client-side under-16 family guidance flow.

It is intentionally scoped to mobile UX only:
- a new welcome-screen entry point
- a deep-linkable `/account-review` flow
- an under-13 parent-or-guardian email path
- a 13-15 parental consent path that tells families to record the video outside the app and email it to `support@divine.video`

- adds a new welcome CTA: `Not 16 yet? That's OK. Here's what you can do.`

- Under no circumstances should a parental consent video be posted on Divine.

issue.title: fix(deep-link): hit Funnelcake REST before relays for /video/<id>
issue.body:
Closes #4178

## Summary

- Cold-start `divine.video/video/<sha256>` deep-links were stuck behind a generic spinner for 60s+ before rendering. Reorders `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` to local cache → Funnelcake REST → relay (each capped by a 3s timeout), so the canonical REST source answers first instead of running last after two relay round-trips that wait for EOSE from disconnected relays.
- Swaps the deep-link loading state from a generic Material `CircularProgressIndicator` to `BrandedLoadingIndicator` (matches the rest of the app).

## Why this was slow

`_VideoRouteCandidate.parse` treats a 64-char hex routeId as **both** an event id and a stable id. The previous flow ran:

1. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(ids:[hash], …)])` — never matches for Blossom-hashed share URLs (kind 34236 event ids are computed differently, the URL hash is the d-tag).
2. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(d:[hash], …)])` — may match.
3. Funnelcake REST.

`NostrClient.queryEvents` waits for EOSE from every relay in the pool with a 5s default timeout, and any relay still mid-connect during cold start blocks the whole batch. The on-relay-ready retry in `VideoDetailScreen` then re-runs the entire sequence on first relay connection. Worst case: ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake + relay-ready wait + ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake = comfortably 60s.

REST is now first because it answers in <1s without waiting on relay state and is the canonical source for divine.video share URLs. Relay is kept as a fallback so events that only live on a user's personal relay still resolve.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/video_detail_screen_test.dart` — 11/11 pass (including updated `BrandedLoadingIndicator` assertions and the cold-start retry test)
- [x] `flutter test packages/videos_repository/` — 322/322 pass, including 4 new `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` tests:
  - resolves shared stable IDs via Funnelcake REST without hitting relay
  - falls back to relay when REST returns null (event only on personal relay)
  - falls back to relay when REST throws (e.g. `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`)
  - returns null without blocking when relay queries hang past the route timeout (verifies the in-source 3s cap fires)
- [ ] Manual: cold-launch app from `https://divine.video/video/c0614bf93911042dc9a3ea571b662ee7e69765e433ecc8468e5a727116577966`, verify branded indicator appears and player renders within ~1–2s.

issue.title: fix(perf): cache BlurhashDisplay decode future across rebuilds
issue.body:
## Description

`BlurhashDisplay` constructed a fresh `_createImageFromPixels(...)` future inside its `build()` method. Each parent rebuild created a new `Future` (different identity), so `FutureBuilder` treated it as a fresh request and re-showed the gradient fallback while the new decode completed. On a 50+ tile profile grid churning under `BackgroundPublishBloc` upload-progress emissions (tracked in #3605), this multiplied into visible flicker across the whole grid plus redundant `decodeImageFromPixels` calls per visible tile.

This was surfaced on low-end Android in @hm21's [review of PR #4191](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4191#pullrequestreview-4257933582), as one of three layers of residual jank that PR's `memCacheWidth` cap didn't address.

### Fix

Cache the decode future in `State` so its identity stays stable across rebuilds, and recompute it only when `blurhash` / `contentType` actually change:

- New `Future<ui.Image?>? _imageFuture` field on `_BlurhashDisplayState`.
- `_decodeBlurhash()` now constructs the future once when new `BlurhashData` arrives, alongside `_blurhashData`, inside the existing `setState`.
- `build()` reads `_imageFuture` instead of constructing a new one each call.

Single-file production change (+12 / -6). Test added pinning the new invariant.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4196

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib/widgets/blurhash_display.dart test/widgets/blurhash_display_test.dart` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/blurhash_display_test.dart` — 1/1 pass (new test asserts `same(future)` across a parent rebuild).
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail_test.dart test/widgets/video_thumbnail_widget_test.dart` — 20/20 pass (existing tests that exercise `BlurhashDisplay` via its callers).
- [ ] Manual: open a profile with **50+ videos** + an active upload (own profile). Confirm gradient fallback no longer flickers across grid tiles during upload-progress ticks. Compare against `main`.

## Related (not addressed here)

- #3605 — `context.watch<BackgroundPublishBloc>` rebuilding the whole grid on every progress tick (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz). Reducing rebuild frequency is the bigger lever; this PR makes each rebuild cheaper while waiting for that fix.
- #3603 — Move profile grid de-duplication out of `build()` (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz).
- #4191 — `memCacheWidth` cap on the network image (decode-cache thrash). Independent layer of the same lag report.

issue.body:
## Summary
- stop the NIP-05 settings screen from spinning forever when the profile load fails
- show retry UI for that failure state instead
- add regression coverage for both the real router navigation path and the profile-load failure path

## Testing
- flutter test --no-pub test/screens/settings/nip05_settings_screen_test.dart
- flutter test --no-pub test/widgets/nostr_settings_screen_test.dart
- flutter test --no-pub test/widgets/nostr_settings_screen_real_nav_test.dart
- flutter analyze

## Context
This is the follow-up to merged PR #4180. The NIP-05 tile navigation works, but the destination screen could mask a profile-load failure behind an infinite loading spinner, which made the tap look like it did nothing.

issue.title: feat: reduce npub prominence on edit profile, add external-account verifier (verifier.divine.video)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## What would you like?

Two related changes to the edit profile experience:

1. **De-emphasize the user's npub on the edit profile screen.** Today the read-only npub is rendered as a labeled top-level `TextFormField` ("Public key (npub)") in the form flow at `mobile/lib/screens/profile_setup_screen.dart:721-759`. The long string dominates the form and pushes more useful fields down. The npub still needs to be available (copy / share / key management) but does not need to be a primary edit-profile field. Some directions for the implementer / design (pick one, not all):
   - Collapse it behind a "Show technical details" disclosure.
   - Move it out of edit profile and into the existing key management screen (`mobile/lib/screens/key_management_screen.dart`).
   - Replace the inline display with a single "Copy public key" action (icon + label, no full string visible by default).

2. **Add an in-app entry point to an external-account verifier.** Where the npub used to live, surface a button/link that opens an in-app webview pointed at `verifier.divine.video` (planned external service). The verifier lets users prove ownership of accounts on other services (e.g. Twitter/X, GitHub, Mastodon, personal websites) tied to their Nostr pubkey. After verification, the verified accounts should be displayable as links on the user's bio/profile.

## How would this be useful for you?

- Edit profile becomes about the things people actually edit (display name, bio, avatar) instead of leading with a 60-character key string most users don't recognize.
- Lets users link out to their existing identities (Twitter, GitHub, Mastodon, personal site) with a verification trail, so followers can trust those links and find them on other platforms.
- Keeps Divine's identity story concrete and user-friendly: "Verify accounts" / "Add verified links to your profile" instead of cryptographic-key-as-UI.

## When would you use this?

- New user finishes onboarding, opens edit profile, and wants to add their existing Twitter/GitHub so people can find them — taps "Verify accounts", goes through the in-app verifier flow, comes back to a profile that shows verified links.
- Existing user wants to migrate their audience from another platform — adds a verified link to their old handle so followers recognize them.

## Scope (what this issue covers)

Mobile-side changes only:

- Reduce npub prominence on the edit profile screen (`profile_setup_screen.dart`).
- Add an entry point ("Verify accounts" / "Add verified links to your profile") that opens an in-app webview using the same pattern Divine already uses for external/integrated apps — **not** an external Safari/Chrome tab.
- Surface verified external accounts as tappable links on the user's bio/profile (read path).
- Follow Divine UI rules: VineTheme, dark-mode only, prefer full-screen flows over new dialogs/sheets.

## Out of scope

- Building / deploying `verifier.divine.video` itself. **This feature depends on that service existing** — flag as a prerequisite.
- Verifying *other people's* external accounts (this issue is only about the current user verifying their own).
- NIP-05 username verification (already exists; see closed #1539, #420).

## Open questions

- **Storage of verified accounts**: are these published as NIP-39 `i` tags on the user's kind 0 profile event (likely fit), as additional kind 0 fields, or fetched separately from a Divine-side service and rendered alongside the profile? Needs product / protocol confirmation before implementation.
- **Verifier handoff contract**: what does the verifier return to the app when the user completes a flow? URL fragment? postMessage? Needs to be defined together with the verifier service.
- **Removal/revocation**: how does a user un-verify or remove a previously verified link? Probably a subsequent profile edit — call out in design.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the edit profile screen, the npub no longer occupies a top-level labeled field; it is reachable via copy action, disclosure, or the key management screen, but not visually dominant.
- [ ] The edit profile screen has an entry point that opens `verifier.divine.video` inside an in-app webview using the existing external-app pattern (not Safari/Chrome).
- [ ] After verification, verified external accounts appear as tappable links on the user's bio/profile.
- [ ] UI follows VineTheme, dark-mode only, full-screen flow preferred.
- [ ] Copy uses brand voice: candid, no jargon (e.g. "Verify accounts", "Add verified links to your profile" — not "Identity attestation").
- [ ] Tests cover the new entry point and the bio rendering of verified links.

## Notes

- Could later be linked under `#599 [Epic] 5. Social Features` or a future profile/identity epic if one is created.
- Related (closed) prior work: #1539 NIP-05 username verification, #420 verified vs display names, #2872 new profile screen layout.

issue.title: fix(deep-link): hit Funnelcake REST before relays for /video/<id>
issue.body:
Closes #4178

## Summary

- Cold-start `divine.video/video/<sha256>` deep-links were stuck behind a generic spinner for 60s+ before rendering. Reorders `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` to local cache → Funnelcake REST → relay (each capped by a 3s timeout), so the canonical REST source answers first instead of running last after two relay round-trips that wait for EOSE from disconnected relays.
- Swaps the deep-link loading state from a generic Material `CircularProgressIndicator` to `BrandedLoadingIndicator` (matches the rest of the app).

## Why this was slow

`_VideoRouteCandidate.parse` treats a 64-char hex routeId as **both** an event id and a stable id. The previous flow ran:

1. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(ids:[hash], …)])` — never matches for Blossom-hashed share URLs (kind 34236 event ids are computed differently, the URL hash is the d-tag).
2. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(d:[hash], …)])` — may match.
3. Funnelcake REST.

`NostrClient.queryEvents` waits for EOSE from every relay in the pool with a 5s default timeout, and any relay still mid-connect during cold start blocks the whole batch. The on-relay-ready retry in `VideoDetailScreen` then re-runs the entire sequence on first relay connection. Worst case: ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake + relay-ready wait + ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake = comfortably 60s.

REST is now first because it answers in <1s without waiting on relay state and is the canonical source for divine.video share URLs. Relay is kept as a fallback so events that only live on a user's personal relay still resolve.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/video_detail_screen_test.dart` — 11/11 pass (including updated `BrandedLoadingIndicator` assertions and the cold-start retry test)
- [x] `flutter test packages/videos_repository/` — 322/322 pass, including 4 new `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` tests:
  - resolves shared stable IDs via Funnelcake REST without hitting relay
  - falls back to relay when REST returns null (event only on personal relay)
  - falls back to relay when REST throws (e.g. `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`)
  - returns null without blocking when relay queries hang past the route timeout (verifies the in-source 3s cap fires)
- [ ] Manual: cold-launch app from `https://divine.video/video/c0614bf93911042dc9a3ea571b662ee7e69765e433ecc8468e5a727116577966`, verify branded indicator appears and player renders within ~1–2s.
